column1: # THE COUPLING EXEMPTIONS (CLAUDE.md, Design rules; project/Coupling.scala `Exemptions`, scripts/ci/coupling_ratchet.py):
# the classes and packages the two limits -- class fan-out (`limit fanout`) and package distance D (`limit distance`,
# packages of `limit distance-min-types` types or more) in test/resources/coupling-baseline.tsv -- do not hold, and the
# declared contracts a class's fan-out counts as ONE dependency. A class or package past a limit with neither a frozen
# baseline row nor a row here fails the push; `scripts/coupling-report --update` never admits it. A row added or loosened
# here lands only in a commit carrying `Coupling: <why>` (the ratchet checks it); a row dropped needs none.
# AN AGENT'S ROW ADDED -- a fan-out row (root, registry, config, class; the owner, 2026-11-19: an agent may add one for a
# genuinely new class past the limit) or a `package` row (the owner, 2026-11-20) -- carries, in the commit adding it: a
# SPECIFIC why, `<role>: <what it does, and why it needs these
# collaborators>` (e.g. `pipeline stage: clusters a family's members; needs the evidence, edges and solver it sequences`;
# 40+ characters and 6+ words besides the class's name; no generic `complex`, `needed`, `for now`, `hard to split`); its
# `added` date (YYYY-MM-DD); and a `Coupling: exempt <Class|package> — <reason>` trailer in the commit's FINAL trailer block.
# `scripts/coupling-report --new-exemptions --since 7d` lists the week's new rows with their reasons and commits. Every
# Monday, .github/workflows/coupling-exemptions.yml puts that list in an owner-assigned issue so he can strike any.
# pattern: a class or package name; `*` matches any run of characters (dots too); `p.*` also matches `p` itself.
#   root        fan-out and distance: the composition roots wire everything and nothing depends on them
#   registry    fan-out: data tables (venue rosters, scraper catalogues) that name one entry per class they list
#   foundation  distance: the bottom layers every package rests on -- stable and concrete on purpose (D near 1 is right)
#   config      fan-out: the typed-config root, which resolves every setting into its typed value in one place
#   class       fan-out: one class past the limit by its role (no `*`): an agent's exemption, its why naming the role
#   package     distance: one package past the limit by its role (no `*`): an agent's exemption, its why naming the role
#               and why its balance of abstractness and stability is right
#               -- the package AS MEASURED: a sub-package without a layer-table row of its own is inside it
#               (services.metrics.web and .worker, under `package services.metrics`); one given such a row is a package
#               of its own, which this row no longer covers, and takes its own row
#   contract    (column 3: the contract's name) the classes matching `pattern` are its USERS: their fan-out counts every
#               member of that contract they use as one dependency
#   member      (column 3: the contract's name) `pattern` is one of the contract's member types -- at most 8 a contract
#               (scripts/ci/coupling_ratchet.py), and adding or dropping one carries `Coupling: <why>` like any loosening
#   contract-size  (pattern: a contract's name; column 3: a number) a contract declared before the 8-member cap,
#               grandfathered at that size: it may not grow, and raising the row is a loosening
# column 3, for the exempting kinds: `exempt`, or a number -- a limit of the class's own, above the shared one.

column5: the composition roots (AppLoader, WorkerMain, AppComponents and the modules.wiring / modules.webwiring traits): every collaboration is wired here (DIP), so their fan-out is the application's size, and their D is a top layer's
command-line programs built from the whole stack like a composition root (FilmwebDiff, RosterAudit)
the review answers' command-line program (`web/runMain services.review.ReviewLabelsCli`): its main wires the mirror client, the answer store and every country's review source like a composition root
a city's or chain's venue roster: one entry a venue, each naming the scraper class that reads it -- data, its fan-out is its row count
a country's scraper catalogue: one entry a source, each naming its client class -- data, its fan-out is its row count
the Polish towns in scrape order: one reference a town's venue roster (pl.venues.*Venues) -- data, its fan-out is its row count
the domain data every layer reads: stable (I near 0) and concrete (A near 0), as values are
generic utilities and the HTTP and Mongo layers, below everything: stable and concrete
typed configuration values, read by every layer: stable and concrete
the title text as a pure function library (TitleNormalizer, FormatTags): stable and concrete, nothing to abstract

metric bundles: concrete series at the system edge, common's shared plumbing (exposition, cache gauges, JVM and tick series) under each tier's own (services.metrics.web, services.metrics.worker), each registering its own Prometheus families; no caller swaps a bundle, so a trait per bundle would be the single-implementation trait CLAUDE.md forbids
the identity model's staging records (StagedCluster, StagedTake, StagingEvent) and their one store, read by the worker's publisher and the web's staging page: stable value types, concrete on purpose

the identity model's value types (Answer, Question, Pin, CandidateQuery, DetailFacts, TitleDecorations, the hashes and memos), read by every identity stage, the agreement stage and the worker's adapters: stable value types, concrete on purpose

stable measured-listing readings, depended on by every stage (the rules, scoring, agreement and the worker's adapters): IdentityMeasures, the *Measures objects, MeasuredListing, Film and Measure as pure functions over values, the Listing they read and the decision values written in them (Candidate, Scored, ResolverDecision, Resolution, DecisionTrace), concrete on purpose

the agreement stages' sources (AgreementStageComposition.Sources): the stores and readers every agreement stage is built from, read together as one unit -- the worker's live ones or a harness's recorded ones, every role filled the same way whoever builds the stage; its builder and the pipeline it fills are written against the unit, one dependency, not eight

the pipeline the composition fills from the sources: it hands each role on to the stage that reads it (the evidence, the held verdicts, the candidates, the takes), so it reads the sources as the one unit the composition hands it
each voter family's answers
the venues' pages and TMDB, two lookups kept apart
the verdicts stored
what was filed since a verdict was read
the posters' hashes
the catalogue's ids
the title text the evidence reads
the clusters' kept keys

pipeline composition: builds, from the agreement sources (one dependency, the `agreement-sources` contract), the stages a model decision is read by (evidence, held verdicts, candidates, inline asks, corrections, takes, cluster verdicts), wires each to what it reads, routes each decision to its stage and keeps each decision's taken-as, digest and event caches across applies; only AgreementStage depends on it

event-driven model host: drains queued scrapes and observations into the IncrementalResolver on one thread through the observation reads, page wait, input gate, listing retainer and history it keeps current, and serves its snapshots to readers

projection orchestrator: sequences read, resolve, scope, draft, guard, write and report (stored films, FilmId map, scoping, drafter, writer, drift, take reports, metrics: one collaborator a stage) and holds only what passes between them: mode, phases, triggers, the index the next projection builds on

projection draft stage: drafts a scope's films from the venue slot source through the slot memo and its persisted fingerprints, the film shapes and the projection index, widens the scope by title keys, and fetches the drafts' TMDB details side by side

store facade: the movies collection and its two side stores (screenings, slots) behind MovieRepository; builds its own pieces (codecs, indexes, side stitch, keyset pages, stitched scan, whole-record upsert, in-place update, stranded-row sweep), keys rows by the title rules and latest year, stamps from its sequence, counts writes and decode failures, audits removals and answers in read outcomes timed by a stopwatch

pipeline root: follows the film change feed and reader into the served read model; sequences the card projection and card store stages, both memos and the screening row writes, reads and writes the read model, gates share cards, is the sweep's seam, logs row drift, anchors cards by the title rules and latest year, and times itself with metrics, a stopwatch and the thread CPU clock

store: the screenings collection over the shared slot-keyed Mongo rows; reads and their outcomes timed by a stopwatch, the slot-keyed addressing and resume-token store its watched change stream uses, the screenings split and stored row it writes, the venue roster guarding each write, and write, decode and screenings metrics

store: the movie_slots collection over the shared slot-keyed Mongo rows; reads and their outcomes timed by a stopwatch, the slot-keyed addressing and resume-token store its watched change stream uses, the stored slot row it writes, the venue roster guarding each write, and write, decode and side-collection change metrics

subscription: the shared movies change stream; owns the listener fan-out and the apply side, opens the movies cursor and two side cursors over the side rows with their reopen driver, resume token and post-image decoder, marks the write fence before re-reads, keeps liveness, answers re-reads as read outcomes and meters change and side events

store role: builds the movies change stream over the Mongo store it is mixed into; hands the stream the store's stamp sequence, write fence, side rows and stitched re-read (a read outcome), a resume token over its token store, a post-image decoder with decode metrics and stopwatch, liveness, and the change, screenings and side metrics

cache: the worker's way into the resident corpus; writes through the repository and its change feed under the write fence, holds the resident corpus with its index and record shape and string pool, attaches the corpus mirror, keys by the title rules, re-kicks enrichment, counts skipped listing writes, audits removals, reads outcomes, and sleeps the lone mirror's retries

account stores: the users and userStates stores (Mongo and in-memory behind the UserRepository and UserStateRepository seams, read-only callers on UserLookup), their codecs, write pipeline, metric bundles and the one AccountDeletion operation; concrete on purpose, since any further trait here would have a single implementation
